The career path for a Customer Success Manager (CSM) at NovaOps follows the support and customer success title ladder, as outlined in the handbook [documents/handbook/titles-for-support.md § Levels]. Here is the typical progression:

- **Current Role: Customer Success Manager (S3)** — Handles complex accounts, coaches teammates, manages difficult conversations, and turns customer feedback into useful internal signals. You own complicated customer situations and make the customer feel heard without overpromising [documents/handbook/titles-for-support.md § Levels].

- **Next Level: S4, Senior Customer Success Manager or Customer Success Director** — Sets quality standards for SupportDesk, creates playbooks for risky situations, reviews Jira escalation quality, builds account-health views, partners with Sales on renewal-risk language, coordinates customer recovery plans, improves onboarding and handoff processes, and coaches managers or senior ICs on support judgment and customer trust [documents/handbook/titles-for-support.md § Levels].

**Promotion Process** — NovaOps promotion cycles run twice per year (March and September). A promotion requires a manager-written packet with evidence from recent work, peer input, and a mapping to the next title level. You need at least six months in your current role, sustained performance, and evidence that you are already operating at the next level [documents/handbook/making-a-career.md § Promotion Process].
